messages:
dmitri: Heads up — while debugging a customer issue I saw console routes surface another org's IDs in the telemetry payloads. small repro below, looks like a meta header is being reused across quick tab switches.

natalie: ugh. can you paste the repro steps + a sample payload? any PII?

 dmitri: steps: 1) log into org A, open app -> /runs 2) quick-switch to org B via topbar 3) open run details -> observe `x-workspace` header for some downstream calls still has org A. sample log: `INFO router: route=/api/exec user=uid-23 x-workspace=org-A x-request-id=...`

 michael: that suggests the route metadata cache key might be missing the workspace id. we use a naive LRU at the console edge: `const cacheKey = user.id + ':' + route` — should include workspace.

 andrea: i pushed a small change last week touching prefetch keys, lemme check. iirc i added `user.context` to the key but maybe not workspace. stepping into it now. :eyes:

 infra-bot: deploy detected: canary/frontend-2024.08.03-rc1 -> staging (started by andrea)

 dmitri: repro includes telemetry payloads sent to ingestion. payload snippet: `{route: "/api/exec", route_meta: {last_tab: "runs"}, headers: {"x-workspace": "org-A", "x-user": "uid-23"}}` — when switching quickly you can see org-A in traces for org-B requests.

 natalie: is this only telemetry or actual data exposure in API responses? customers noticed ghost rows?

 dmitri: telemetry + some UI flashes. i saw list endpoints returning rows from previous org in the local cache layer for ~1s after switch. likely client-side combined with stale KV prefix.

 michael: root cause hypothesis: prefetch/cache key composition mismatch between router and client-edge cache. router routes by `x-workspace` but cache entries are keyed by `user.id:route` so when user context swaps, old entry is returned until refreshed.

 andrea: confirm — my change touched `prefetchKey` function in app-shell. quick diff: `- return [user.id, route].join(':')
+ return [user.id, route, user.context].join(':')` but `user.context` sometimes contains `{org: 'org-A'}` and the router expects `workspace` string. mismatch.

 dmitri: nice find. so two problems: inconsistent field names (context vs workspace) and some caches storing headers instead of explicit workspace id.

 natalie: action items: 1) patch prefetchKey to use canonical `workspaceId` (and add tests) 2) add router-side validation to refuse serving stale entries when `x-workspace` header != cache.workspace 3) run a retroactive telemetry query to estimate exposure window and affected org count.

 andrea: i'll open a PR for (1) + tests. will also revert the `user.context` usage in hotpath. PR in ~20m :thumbsup:

 michael: for (2) we can add a cheap header check at the edge: when serving from cache include cached-workspace meta and compare to `x-workspace` header. if mismatch, treat as miss and refresh. cheap and safe. i'll draft the router patch.

 jason: priority = P1 for prod rollback risk. if any chance real user data leaked beyond UI flashes, we need to triage and notify security/compliance. natalie, can you own telemetry query and coordinate with security?

 natalie: on it. query i'm running: `SELECT count(distinct org_id) as orgs, min(ts), max(ts) FROM console_telemetry WHERE event='route_serve' AND cached_workspace != header_workspace GROUP BY 1` — will run and share numbers.

 dmitri: added a tiny repro snippet for QA: `curl -H "x-workspace: org-A" -H "cookie: session=abc" /api/prefetch && quick-switch && curl -H "x-workspace: org-B" -H "cookie: session=abc" /api/list` watch logs for `cached_workspace=org-A`.

 andrea: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/frontend/pull/4123 — fixes key to `workspaceId` and adds unit test for quick-switch.

 infra-bot: deploy plan created: frontend/hotfix-key-normalize -> canary -> prod (manual approve)

 michael: opened router PR too: https://git.internal/redwood/router/pull/287 — adds strict workspace check on cache hits + metric `cache_workspace_mismatch`

 natalie: telemetry run results (rough): `cache_workspace_mismatch` events ~47k in last 24h, affected orgs ~12, median exposure window ~800ms. i'm escalating to sec + customer success.

 jason: thanks team. steps for rollforward: andrea's PR + michael's router change -> canary -> watch `cache_workspace_mismatch` -> if drops to 0 proceed to prod. also prepare customer comms template if we need to notify orgs.

 dmitri: thanks all. leaving a note in the incident channel with the repro and PR links. will follow up on any CS asks. :shipit:
